subject: [hw] T01 -> lead: V19 overlap fix confirmed -- patching all V19 source reads makes arm-O2 go to 0 mismatches except k_v15_extend 5
body:
I applied a **test-only** change to a /tmp copy of n2a32_neon_shift.c: snapshot the whole CPU at entry and make every source read (`vec_get` and the direct `elem_get(&c->d[...])` sites at lines ~133,583,718/719,800,845/846,892,959,986) read the snapshot; writes still go to the live CPU. Result with the 139-kernel arm-O2 corpus, 20 seeds each:

  before: 125 mismatches (k_i8_loop, k_i16_loop, k_i16_mul, k_neon_vmla16, k_neon_vsubl, k_u8_sad, k_v15_extend)
  after:   5 mismatches, only k_v15_extend (5/20 seeds)

So the V19 overlap bug is real and is the root of the vector red; the fix is to snapshot the source operands (128 bits) before writing Vd, or buffer results until the loop ends. There is already a 128-bit local in each op; the simplest is a `struct n2a32_cpu snap = *c;` at the top of each op function and read from it, or one per n2a32_neon_shift call. I can send the exact /tmp diff, but it is not in the tree because V19 owns the file. Please apply/authorize. k_v15_extend still fails 5/20 after this; its code uses VTST+VMOVN.I16 and VFP lane extracts, all of which pass isolated, so it may be a second small issue. V14 patch also still unapplied; with it thumb-O0 is 0 mismatches over 139 kernels.
